papers.title: Same margin, different lesion: margin subtype, glandular involvement, and endocervical curettage status as predictors of residual CIN2+ at repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure: An 11-year retrospective cohort study.
papers.abstract: OBJECTIVE: The aim of this study was to assess how initial loop electrosurgical excision procedure margin subtype, glandular involvement, endocervical curettage findings, and specimen size relate to re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure pathology and receipt of further surgery. METHODS: In this retrospective cohort study, 287 patients undergoing re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure at a tertiary center (2015-2025) were reviewed. Initial margin status was classified as margin continuity, margin adjacency, or non-evaluable margin. Associations with re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure pathology, residual CIN2+ disease, and receipt of a third surgical intervention were assessed using chi-square/Fisher-Freeman-Halton tests, Cohen's kappa, and multivariate logistic regression. RESULTS: Initial and re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure pathology showed a significant group-level association (p=0.039) but no case-by-case agreement beyond chance (kappa=-0.009, p=0.754); most patients with initial CIN2/3 had CIN1 at re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure. Margin adjacency independently predicted residual CIN2+ disease at repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure (OR 11.045, p=0.049), as did glandular involvement (OR 1.938, p=0.035). Among patients with negative re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure margins, residual CIN2+ disease was identified within the specimen in 27.1%, and human papillomavirus test negativity at the first follow-up visit was 88.2%, varying by genotype. Positive margin (OR 333.33, p<0.001) and positive endocervical curettage (OR 41.67, p<0.001) at repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure were the strongest predictors of receiving a third surgical intervention. CONCLUSION: Margin adjacency and glandular involvement independently predicted residual CIN2+ at repeat loop electrosurgical excision procedure, whereas positive margins and positive endocervical curettage at re-loop electrosurgical excision procedure were strongly associated with receipt of a third surgical intervention. Post-loop electrosurgical excision procedure follow-up should integrate margin subtype, glandular involvement, endocervical curettage findings, and human papillomavirus surveillance rather than rely on margin status alone; genotype-specific differences in human papillomavirus test negativity require confirmation in larger cohorts.

papers.abstract_zh: 目的:本研究的目的是评估初始环形电外科切除术边缘亚型、腺体受累、宫颈内膜刮除结果和标本大小与再次环形电外科切除术病理学和接受进一步手术的关系。方法:在这项回顾性 队列研究 研究中,回顾了 287 名在三级中心(2015-2025 年)接受再循环电外科切除手术的患者。初始保证金状态分为保证金连续性、保证金相邻性或不可评估保证金。使用卡方/Fisher-Freeman-Halton 检验、Cohen's kappa 和多变量逻辑回归评估与再循环电外科切除手术病理学、残留 CIN2+ 疾病和接受第三次手术干预的关联。结果:初始和再次循环电外科切除手术病理学显示出显着的组级相关性(p=0.039),但除偶然性外没有个案一致性(kappa=-0.009,p=0.754);大多数初始 CIN2/3 的患者在再次循环电外科切除过程中出现 CIN1。边缘邻近独立预测重复循环电外科切除过程中残留的 CIN2+ 疾病(OR 11.045,p=0.049),腺体受累也是如此(OR 1.938,p=0.035)。在再次循环电外科切除手术边缘呈阴性的患者中,27.1% 的标本内发现残留 CIN2+ 疾病,首次随访时 人乳头瘤病毒 测试阴性的率为 88.2%,具体情况因基因型而异。重复循环电外科切除过程中的阳性切缘(OR 333.33,p<0.001)和阳性宫颈管刮除术(OR 41.67,p<0.001)是接受第三次手术干预的最强预测因素。结论:边缘邻近和腺体受累独立预测重复环路电外科切除手术中残留的 CIN2+,而再次环路电外科切除手术中的阳性切缘和阳性宫颈管刮除术与接受第三次手术干预密切相关。环路电外科切除术后随访应综合切缘亚型、腺体受累、宫颈管刮除结果和 人乳头瘤病毒 监测,而不是仅依赖切缘状态;人乳头瘤病毒 测试阴性的基因型特异性差异需要在较大的 队列研究 中进行确认。

news.content: Saturday, 14 November 2026, 05:43:44 am Toggle navigation Home National World Kashmir Current Affairs Programs FM 101 Urdu Dictionary CGTN Saut-ul-Quran Toggle navigation Podcast SIFC Ahang HPV vaccination drive to begin across KP on Wednesday November 08, 2026 Health authorities have urged parents to ensure that their daughters aged 9 to 14 years receive vaccination against human papillomavirus (HPV) during an upcoming immunization campaign across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa. The campaign will run from Wednesday until the 24th of this month and aims to protect adolescent girls against HPV, the primary cause of cervical cancer, through the administration of a safe and effective vaccine. Parents seeking further information about the vaccination drive and related services have been advised to contact the Sehat Tahaffuz helpline at 1166. They said the initiative is part of ongoing efforts to strengthen preventive healthcare and raise awareness about cervical cancer, which remains a major public health concern among women. More News World Diabetes Day to be observed tomorrow World Immunization Day observed Int’l Day of Radiology observed Pakistan, Türkiye make significant progress in local vaccine production Sohail Mahmood highlights importance of D-8 health cooperation

news.title_zh: HPV 疫苗接种 活动将于周三开始穿过 KP
news.source_body_en: The news report highlights the initiation of an HPV vaccination drive across Khyber Pakhtunkhwa (KP) starting on Wednesday, November 10, 2026, and running until November 24, 2026. The campaign targets adolescent girls aged 9 to 14 years to protect them against human papillomavirus (HPV), a primary cause of cervical cancer. Health authorities have urged parents to ensure their daughters receive the vaccine during this period. The initiative is part of broader efforts to enhance preventive healthcare and raise awareness about cervical cancer, which remains a significant public health concern. Parents seeking more information are advised to contact the Sehat Tahaffuz helpline at 1166. The campaign is currently underway, and no specific case or death counts are reported in the evidence. The source is a partial report from Bing News RSS, published on November 8, 2026.
news.content_zh: 该新闻报道强调,从 2026 年 11 月 10 日星期三开始,在开伯尔-普赫图赫瓦省 (KP) 启动了 HPV 疫苗接种 活动,一直持续到 2026 年 11 月 24 日。该活动针对 9 至 14 岁的少女,保护她们免受 人乳头瘤病毒 (HPV) 感染,这是导致 宫颈癌 的主要原因。卫生当局敦促家长确保他们的女儿在此期间获得 疫苗。该举措是加强预防性医疗保健和提高对 宫颈癌 认识的更广泛努力的一部分,宫颈癌 仍然是一个重大的公共卫生问题。建议寻求更多信息的家长拨打 Sehat Tahaffuz 帮助热线 1166。该活动目前正在进行中,证据中没有报告具体病例或死亡人数。来源是 Bing News RSS 的部分报道,于 2026 年 11 月 8 日发布。

Search Search Home News PAHO secures first-ever region-wide access agreements for HPV testing across Latin America and the Caribbean, with support from Unitaid PAHO secures first-ever region-wide access agreements for HPV testing across Latin America and the Caribbean, with support from Unitaid Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Opens in a new window Landmark regional agreements will lower costs of high-quality HPV testing and help more women benefit from effective cervical cancer screening. Washington, D.C./Geneva, 11 November 2026 — Millions of women across Latin America and the Caribbean will gain access to more affordable, high-quality human papillomavirus (HPV) testing under landmark regional access agreements negotiated by the Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) through its Regional Revolving Funds. Unitaid supported these efforts to expand access to HPV testing and will advance implementation activities in selected countries. HPV infection causes nearly all cases of cervical cancer, which kills more than 40,000 women in the region each year. Cervical cancer is highly preventable through vaccination, screening and timely treatment. Until now, countries across Latin America and the Caribbean have faced some of the highest HPV test prices in the world. Under these first-ever regional access agreements, countries will be able to access high-quality molecular HPV tests through preferential pricing and a comprehensive support package, with participating countries expected to realize cost savings ranging from 30% to 70%. These technologies are now available through PAHO's Revolving Fund under harmonized regional conditions for all countries and territories in Latin America and the Caribbean. The arrangements expand the range of WHO-recommended molecular HPV testing technologies available through PAHO's Revolving Funds. In addition to access to testing, the agreements include implementation support, equipment access, training, maintenance and technical assistance designed to facilitate country adoption and scale-up. By building these components together, the agreements help to reduce operational barriers that have often limited the introduction of new diagnostic technologies. PAHO/WHO has recommended the use of HPV testing in cervical cancer screening programs since 2013, with updated guidance issued in 2026. However, uptake in the region has been limited due to financial, technical, and programmatic barriers. Unitaid's support to PAHO translates into expanded access to HPV testing in the region. Unitaid will also support implementation activities in El Salvador, Guatemala, Grenada, Saint Vincent and the Grenadines, and Saint Lucia, helping countries to introduce or expand HPV-based screening programs while strengthening follow-up care for women with positive results. "Through PAHO's Revolving Funds, countries now have access to high-quality HPV testing under more favorable conditions, helping accelerate efforts to eliminate cervical cancer in the Americas," said PAHO Director Dr. Jarbas Barbosa. "These agreements reflect PAHO's commitment to working with Member States and partners to expand equitable access to essential health technologies and strengthen cervical cancer prevention programs across the Region." “These agreements build on Unitaid’s global efforts to make cervical cancer prevention more affordable and accessible for women everywhere,” said Dr. Philippe Duneton, Executive Director of Unitaid. “By expanding access to affordable, high-quality HPV testing in Latin America and the Caribbean, and extending favorable pricing to countries that have historically been excluded from such arrangements, this initiative helps accelerate progress toward cervical cancer elimination while creating a more equitable and sustainable market for screening technologies.” Molecular tests directly detect high-risk HPV types responsible for most cervical cancer cases, allowing for early identification of women at risk. Compared to other screening methods, they perform better and can use self-collected samples, which can help expand access to testing among underserved populations. The ESTAMPA study, conducted in Latin America, found that HPV testing detected nearly all cases of precancerous cervical lesions and invasive cancer, while cytology, the conventional screening method, identified fewer than half of the cases. This highlights significant gaps between the accuracy of these two methods. Expanding the use of HPV tests is key to advancing toward the WHO’s global cervical cancer elimination targets – known as the 90-70-90 goals: 90% of girls vaccinated against HPV, 70% of women screened with a high-performance test, and 90% of women with lesions appropriately treated. Currently, 16 countries and territories in Latin America and the Caribbean have introduced HPV testing in their screening programs, although coverage has been limited by the high cost of the tests. The new access to molecular HPV tests through the Revolving Funds is part of PAHO’s Disease Elimination Initiative, which seeks to eliminate more than 30 diseases and related conditions in the Americas, including cervical cancer. It also forms part of the Better Care for NCDs initiative, designed to strengthen health systems and integrate prevention and control of these diseases into primary care. Unitaid’s cervical cancer elimination efforts in Latin America are made possible through contributions from the Government of Japan, alongside support from Unitaid’s other core donors Brazil, Chile, France, the Gates Foundation, Norway, Portugal, the Republic of Korea, Spain and the United Kingdom. About PAHO The Pan American Health Organization (PAHO) works with the countries of the Americas to improve the health and quality of life of its population. Founded in 1902, it is the world’s oldest international public health agency. It serves as the Regional Office of WHO for the Americas and is the specialized health agency of the Inter-American system (OAS). For more information about PAHO and its work, please visit: www.paho.org About Unitaid Unitaid saves lives by making new health products affordable and available in low- and middle-income countries. Collaborating with partners, Unitaid identifies innovative treatments, tackles market barriers, and quickly delivers solutions to those in need. Since 2006, Unitaid has unlocked over 150 health products, addressing HIV, TB, malaria, women’s and children’s health, and pandemic preparedness. Every year, these products benefit more than 300 million people. Unitaid is a hosted partnership of the World Health Organization. www.unitaid.org Media contacts PAHO: Sebastian Oliel: +1 202 316-5679 / Ashley Baldwin: + 1 202 340-4025 - mediateam@paho.org Unitaid: Kyle Wilkinson, +41 79 445 17 45, wilkinsonk@unitaid.who.int News Releases Cancer Adolescent Health Cervical cancer Immunization Brasil United States of America Puerto Rico Noncommunicable Diseases and Mental Health (NMH) It's Time to End Cervical Cancer Diseases Elimination Initiative Better Care for NCDs Initiative Human Papillomavirus (HPV) Vaccine Latest news Public university hospitals in the Americas to develop regional alliance to strengthen health systems 13 Nov 2026 Diabetes in the Americas: 112 million adults live with the disease as gaps in diagnosis and treatment persist 12 Nov 2026 PAHO secures first-ever region-wide access agreements for HPV testing across Latin America and the Caribbean, with support from Unitaid 11 Nov 2026 See all the news

elements_zh.location_and_population: 这些协议涵盖拉丁美洲和加勒比地区的所有国家和地区,并计划为萨尔瓦多、危地马拉、格林纳达、圣文森特和格林纳丁斯以及圣卢西亚提供具体实施支持。受影响的人口包括该地区数百万妇女。

steps up efforts to eliminate cervical cancer: from listening to communities to developing solutions to save lives Cabo Verde steps up efforts to eliminate cervical cancer: from listening to communities to developing solutions to save lives 10 November 2026 | News Release | Reading time: 7 min Cabo Verde steps up efforts to eliminate cervical cancer: from listening to communities to developing solutions to save lives More pictures More images Praia, Cabo Verde – In an archipelagic country such as Cabo Verde, ensuring that all women have access to screening, diagnosis and timely treatment for cervical cancer requires responses tailored to different local realities. The country’s insularity, the challenges of referral and the need to ensure continuity of care make it particularly important to organise accessible, integrated services centred on women’s needs. It is against this backdrop that Cabo Verde is stepping up its efforts to accelerate the elimination of cervical cancer as a public health problem, through an initiative led by the Ministry of Health, with technical assistance from the World Health Organisation (WHO) and financial support from the Spanish Government, via the Spanish Agency for International Development Cooperation (AECID). The initiative aims to support the development of a National Acceleration Plan to consolidate the progress made, strengthen the capacity of health services and translate international commitments into concrete and sustainable interventions. It also includes strengthening technical capacity, updating clinical protocols, providing additional equipment and consumables, and developing a communication and awareness-raising strategy. Listening to bring about change: 12 field visits and around 60 people involved During October 2026, a WHO technical mission, working in close collaboration with the Ministry of Health, carried out 12 field visits and consulted around 60 people, including health professionals, community leaders, representatives from the private sector, non-governmental organisations, programmes run by the National Health Directorate and partner institutions. The mission prioritised a participatory approach, seeking to understand existing capacities, identifying the main constraints and gather input to develop solutions tailored to the national context. Boa Vista Island: bringing screening closer to women and strengthening local capacities On the island of Boa Vista, chosen for the implementation of the pilot project, visits were made to the Health Centre, the laboratory facility, the Maternal and Child Health Service and a private health clinic, which enabled a more in-depth analysis of the conditions necessary for implementing an organised screening pilot project. Discussions with community associations and other local stakeholders also highlighted the importance of community involvement in raising awareness and mobilising women. The project aims to increase the uptake of human papillomavirus (HPV) screening tests, strengthening mechanisms for identifying and inviting women to participate in screening, and establish a care pathway that ensures continuity of care from screening through to diagnosis and, where necessary, treatment. Key needs identified include improving the availability and use of data for decision-making, defining effective strategies to encourage women to take part in screening, and establishing clear flowcharts for follow-up, referral and monitoring. For Dr Risete Gomes, Health Officer for Boa Vista ai, this initiative opens up new prospects for the island, particularly in the field of women’s health. She emphasised the importance of ensuring clear, consistent and standardised communication between healthcare professionals and service users, in order to improve understanding of the screening programme, its benefits and the need for follow-up. She also highlighted the need to strengthen the capacity of healthcare staff, considering this essential to guaranteeing the quality of services and the sustainable implementation of the project. The experience on Boa Vista should enable the testing of mechanisms for organising screening, communication, registration and follow-up of women, yielding lessons that could guide the gradual expansion of the initiative to other islands. The initiative is scheduled to begin in 2027 and aims to reach a target population of an estimated 1,500 women. National leadership and commitment to elimination The technical workshop held on 21 October 2026 in the city of Praia provided an important opportunity to analyse the challenges identified and discuss the priorities for drawing up the National Acceleration Plan. On that occasion, Dr Heidy Teixeira, representing the Minister of Health, reaffirmed Cape Verde’s commitment to aligning the national response with the WHO Global Strategy to Accelerate the Elimination of Cervical Cancer as a Public Health Problem. Recognising that there is still a long way to go, she emphasised the need to accelerate interventions, consolidate the progress made and strengthen an integrated and sustainable national response. Among the advances achieved, she highlighted the fact that the target of 90 per cent HPV vaccination coverage among girls had been exceeded, and that boys had been included in the national vaccination strategy. These results provide an important foundation for stepping up efforts in the other components of the elimination strategy, particularly screening, early diagnosis and treatment. In her address, the WHO Representative in Cabo Verde, Dr Ann Lindstrand, congratulated the Ministry of Health on its leadership of the process and reaffirmed the Organisation’s commitment to continuing to support the country in realising this public health priority. The Representative emphasised the importance of ensuring that interventions reach all islands and communities, leaving no woman behind. “Eliminating cervical cancer as a public health problem is an achievable ambition. But it requires us to turn knowledge into action and commitments into concrete results.” She also emphasised that the provision of equipment, whilst essential, must be accompanied by capacity-building for healthcare professionals, the establishment of effective referral pathways, access to treatment, and information systems capable of monitoring outcomes. The financial partnership with AECID represents a significant contribution to the realisation of this initiative. During his address at the workshop, Fernando Regúlez, a representative of AECID, highlighted the importance of the financial partnership between the Spanish Government, the WHO and Cape Verde in supporting national efforts to eliminate cervical cancer. This collaboration demonstrates the value of strategic partnerships in mobilising resources and strengthening national capacities, helping to translate public health priorities into concrete actions. One of the highlights of this workshop was the symbolic handover of HPV DNA test kits, equipment and consumables to support the roll-out of the pilot project in Boa Vista. The technical mission in October 2026 made it possible to gather evidence, identify operational needs and mobilise different stakeholders around a common vision: to build a more organised, accessible and sustainable national response. The next steps include consolidating the National Acceleration Plan, the operational preparation of the pilot project in Boa Vista, training professionals, defining mechanisms for reaching out to women, and developing tools for registration, referral and monitoring. The true impact of this initiative will be measured by its ability to translate these priorities into concrete improvements in access to and the quality of services, ensuring that every woman identified can undergo screening, receive her results and benefit from timely follow-up and treatment where necessary. With national leadership, technical support from the WHO, financial partnership from AECID and the involvement of health professionals and communities, Cape Verde is laying the foundations to accelerate the elimination of cervical cancer as a public health problem. Because eliminating cervical cancer also means reducing inequalities, protecting lives and ensuring that no woman is left behind. news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 14, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Study Uncovers Distinct Age-Related Drivers of HPV Infection in Western Zambia by November 12, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 2 mins read 0 Study Uncovers Distinct Age-Related Drivers of HPV Infection in Western Zambia Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A cross-sectional investigation conducted among women attending cervical cancer screening clinics in Western Province, Zambia, has revealed comparable rates of high-risk human papillomavirus (HPV) infection across age groups alongside markedly distinct risk factors. The study, carried out between October 2025 and January 2026, enrolled 1,132 participants using consecutive sampling to examine the prevalence and determinants of infection. Overall, the researchers detected an HPV prevalence of 33.6 percent, noting virtually identical burdens among younger and older demographics. Specifically, women aged 40 years and younger exhibited an infection rate of 33.6 percent, whereas participants aged 41 years and older had an infection rate of 33.4 percent. To obtain these clinical measurements, healthcare teams collected exfoliated cervical specimens from the participants and screened for high-risk HPV genotypes using the Hologic Panther platform paired with transcription-mediated amplification (TMA). In parallel, investigators administered structured questionnaires to capture detailed sociodemographic, behavioural, and reproductive information from each woman. To account for potential clustering of outcomes across different health facilities in the province, the analytical team applied mixed-effects logistic regression models to identify factors independently associated with viral infection. The statistical analyses revealed that the independent determinants of HPV infection diverged significantly depending on participant age. Among women aged 40 years and younger, infection was independently associated with a higher number of lifetime sexual partners, high parity, lack of HPV vaccination, contraceptive use, low income, single marital status, and attendance at rural healthcare facilities (P < 0.05). In contrast, among women aged 41 years and older, the independent risk factors comprised high parity, low HPV knowledge, unemployment, low income, and broader geographic location (P < 0.05). Beyond age-stratified predictors, the research group documented spatial variations in infection frequency across the study region, observing significantly elevated HPV rates within Mwandi district. The investigators noted that Zambia continues to experience one of the highest cervical cancer burdens globally, where human papillomavirus persists as a leading cause of cervical malignancy in low- and middle-income settings. In interpreting these patterns, the authors indicated that the substantial regional burden of HIV and ongoing transmission dynamics may also play a role in sustaining high levels of HPV infection across age groups. Reflecting on these contrasting associations, the study authors emphasize that interventions should be tailored to address the unique drivers identified within each age demographic. Rather than applying a uniform approach, the findings support integrated, age-specific prevention initiatives that combine HPV vaccination, routine cervical cancer screening, health education, and clinical treatment services to effectively curb the burden of HPV infection and its long-term health consequences across Western Province. news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 14, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Lianyungang Study Finds Eighteen Percent Overall Human Papillomavirus Infection Rate by November 12, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Lianyungang Study Finds Eighteen Percent Overall Human Papillomavirus Infection Rate Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A retrospective analysis of 50,279 women at Lianyungang Maternal and Child Health Hospital identified an overall human papillomavirus infection rate of 18.57 percent, representing 9,336 positive cases diagnosed between 2021 and 2025 in Northern Jiangsu Province, China. Longitudinal surveillance over the five-year evaluation period revealed fluctuations in annual detection, with the infection rate rising from 15.30 percent in 2021 to a peak of 21.18 percent in 2023, before adjusting to 19.84 percent by 2025. Evaluation of viral infection patterns indicated that single infections predominated across the positive cohort, accounting for 75.83 percent of cases with 7,080 infected women displaying a single viral genotype. Discover more Check Symptoms Book a Checkup Read Med Journals Find Cancer Care Analysis of age-stratified positivity demonstrated a bimodal distribution across demographic groups, reaching a first peak of 23.56 percent (810 of 3,438) among women aged 25 years or younger and a second peak of 26.05 percent (1,017 of 3,904) among women aged 56 years or older. Genotyping identified HPV52 as the most frequent variant with a prevalence of 3.62 percent (1,822 of 50,279), followed by HPV16 at 3.01 percent (1,514 of 50,279), HPV58 at 2.46 percent (1,239 of 50,279), HPV53 at 1.97 percent (989 of 50,279), and HPV39 at 1.72 percent (864 of 50,279), while HPV81 represented the most prevalent low-risk genotype at 1.70 percent (856 of 50,279). Annual genotype tracking showed that HPV53 prevalence increased significantly from 1.51 percent in 2021 to 2.72 percent in 2025 (P < 0.001), providing the largest localized epidemiological dataset to date to guide regional cervical cancer prevention and control strategies in Lianyungang. The clinical objective of the investigation centered on analyzing both the prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus infection across the population of Lianyungang, located in Northern Jiangsu Province, China. By systematically characterizing these viral patterns, the research was designed to provide localized epidemiological data necessary to support the prevention and treatment of cervical cancer and related diseases throughout the municipality. Discover more Study Biology infections Infection infection Buy Maps To evaluate these dynamics, the study design relied on a retrospective analysis of HPV genotyping records collected from 50,279 women at Lianyungang Maternal and Child Health Hospital between 2021 and 2025. The methodological evaluation systematically examined four distinct epidemiological parameters across the five-year surveillance period: overall infection rates, viral genotype distribution, age-specific positivity across demographic cohorts, and multi-year longitudinal trends. The research team concluded that the investigation provides the largest-scale dataset compiled to date regarding recent human papillomavirus epidemiology in Lianyungang. The authors noted that these localized empirical findings are intended to guide public health authorities in the development and implementation of regional cervical cancer prevention and disease control strategies. In evaluating the composition of positive cases, the researchers observed that solitary viral detection predominated over concurrent strains. The age-stratified data demonstrated that infection risk was concentrated at opposite extremes of the tested demographic spectrum. Women aged 56 years and older recorded the highest positivity rate across all evaluated groups at 26.05 percent (1,017 of 3,904), exceeding the initial peak of 23.56 percent (810 of 3,438) identified among women aged 25 years or younger. Regarding viral heterogeneity across the full sample of 50,279 women, the genotype hierarchy revealed distinct frequencies among dominant variants. HPV52 emerged as the most prevalent genotype at 3.62 percent (1,822 cases), followed by HPV16 at 3.01 percent (1,514 cases) and HPV58 at 2.46 percent (1,239 cases). HPV53 and HPV39 accounted for 1.97 percent (989 cases) and 1.72 percent (864 cases), respectively. In addition to these leading variants, the evaluation specifically classified HPV81 as the most common low-risk human papillomavirus genotype, affecting 1.70 percent of women (856 cases). analysis.location_and_population: The study focused on Lianyungang, Northern Jiangsu Province, China, involving 50,279 women at Lianyungang Maternal and Child Health Hospital (N1, N7, N9).
analysis.event: A retrospective analysis of HPV genotyping records identified an overall infection rate of 18.57 percent among women in Lianyungang, with 9,336 positive cases diagnosed between 2021 and 2025 (N1, N9).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study found a bimodal age distribution of HPV infection, with the highest positivity rate among women aged 56 years or older at 26.05 percent (1,017 of 3,904) and among women aged 25 years or younger at 23.56 percent (810 of 3,438). HPV52 was the most frequent variant at 3.62 percent (1,822 cases), followed by HPV16 at 3.01 percent (1,514 cases) and HPV58 at 2.46 percent (1,239 cases). Single infections predominated, accounting for 75.83 percent of cases (N1, N4, N15, N17, N19).
analysis.response_status_and_uncertainty: The research aimed to provide localized epidemiological data to guide cervical cancer prevention and control strategies. It included longitudinal trends and genotype distribution analysis, with HPV53 prevalence increasing significantly from 1.51 percent in 2021 to 2.72 percent in 2025 (N6, N10, N12).

news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 14, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Vaginal Neoplasia Shows High HPV Genotype Concordance With Prior Genital Lesions by November 11, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Vaginal Neoplasia Shows High HPV Genotype Concordance With Prior Genital Lesions Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram Direct tissue-based testing of archived clinical specimens has revealed that secondary vaginal intraepithelial lesions share identical human papillomavirus genotypes with earlier lower genital tract neoplasia in the vast majority of cases. In an investigation tracking paired tissue samples across intervals spanning up to 31.8 years, 96.4 percent of evaluable cases shared at least one viral genotype between initial and subsequent neoplastic sites. The findings demonstrate that women diagnosed with high-grade vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia frequently harbor the exact viral types identified in their previous genital tract disease, providing concrete tissue-level evidence consistent with long-term viral persistence or reactivation. Women who undergo treatment for human papillomavirus-associated neoplasia in the cervix or other lower genital tract locations face a well-recognized ongoing risk of later developing vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia, categorized clinically as VaIN. Despite this established clinical vulnerability, direct molecular data confirming whether secondary vaginal lesions arise from the same persistent virus or from new, independent viral exposures have historically remained limited. To evaluate this question, researchers utilized archived pathological specimens to perform lesion-specific human papillomavirus genotyping, comparing tissue from advanced vaginal lesions against paired historical specimens from earlier lower genital tract neoplasia. The study was designed as a retrospective, single-center cohort investigation conducted at University Hospital Královské Vinohrady in Prague, Czech Republic, operating under institutional ethics approval reference number EK-VP/34/00/2025. Investigators identified a cohort of 72 eligible women with histologically confirmed and human papillomavirus-associated VaIN2+, a classification encompassing grade 2 or grade 3 vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia as well as invasive vaginal carcinoma. Among the 72 enrolled patients, 39 women, representing 54.2 percent of the study cohort, had documented medical histories of prior human papillomavirus-associated lower genital tract neoplasia. Discover more Find an OBGYN Find Cancer Care See an OB-GYN genotypes Order DNA Kits Laboratory evaluations focused on archived formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue blocks processed through a multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction assay to identify specific viral genotypes. Valid vaginal lesion genotyping was successfully achieved in 56 women, comprising 30 patients who had a history of prior lower genital tract neoplasia and 26 patients presenting without preceding neoplastic disease. Across all lesions with valid testing results, human papillomavirus genotype 16 predominated, detected in 51.8 percent of cases. Furthermore, statistical analysis demonstrated that human papillomavirus 16 was independently associated with the development of severe VaIN3+ lesions, carrying an adjusted odds ratio of 3.84 with a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.22 to 12.93 and a p-value of 0.024. Direct genotype concordance was specifically assessed in a subset of 28 patients for whom paired tissue specimens from both the original and secondary lesions were available, evaluable, and positive for human papillomavirus. Within this paired group, complete viral concordance was established in 23 women (82.1 percent), partial concordance in four women (14.3 percent), and an absence of concordance in only one woman (3.6 percent). When examining exploratory clinical contrasts, combined positivity for human papillomavirus 16 and 18 occurred more frequently among women with prior neoplasia compared to those without (66.7 percent versus 38.5 percent; p = 0.059), as did VaIN3+ diagnoses (66.7 percent versus 42.3 percent; p = 0.106); however, neither difference remained statistically significant below the 0.05 threshold following adjustment for multiplicity. The research team concluded that the pronounced frequency of shared viral genotypes strongly aligns with long-term viral persistence or subsequent reactivation of the primary human papillomavirus genotype over decades. Nevertheless, the investigators highlighted essential methodological limitations: reinfection with the identical viral genotype over time cannot be definitively excluded, and the analysis did not evaluate whether the paired lesions shared a common clonal origin. Given the extended latency intervals observed between primary and secondary neoplastic diagnoses, the study authors emphasized that these findings reinforce the necessity of extended, long-term surveillance protocols for women who have received treatment for high-grade cervical and lower genital tract lesions. In an investigation tracking paired tissue samples across intervals spanning up to 31.8 years, 96.4 percent of evaluable cases shared at least one viral genotype between initial and subsequent neoplastic sites. The findings demonstrate that women diagnosed with high-grade vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia frequently harbor the exact viral types identified in their previous genital tract disease, providing concrete tissue-level evidence consistent with long-term viral persistence or reactivation. Women who undergo treatment for human papillomavirus-associated neoplasia in the cervix or other lower genital tract locations face a well-recognized ongoing risk of later developing vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia, categorized clinically as VaIN. Despite this established clinical vulnerability, direct molecular data confirming whether secondary vaginal lesions arise from the same persistent virus or from new, independent viral exposures have historically remained limited. To evaluate this question, researchers utilized archived pathological specimens to perform lesion-specific human papillomavirus genotyping, comparing tissue from advanced vaginal lesions against paired historical specimens from earlier lower genital tract neoplasia. The study was designed as a retrospective, single-center cohort investigation conducted at University Hospital Královské Vinohrady in Prague, Czech Republic, operating under institutional ethics approval reference number EK-VP/34/00/2025. Investigators identified a cohort of 72 eligible women with histologically confirmed and human papillomavirus-associated VaIN2+, a classification encompassing grade 2 or grade 3 vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia as well as invasive vaginal carcinoma. Among the 72 enrolled patients, 39 women, representing 54.2 percent of the study cohort, had documented medical histories of prior human papillomavirus-associated lower genital tract neoplasia. Discover more Find an OBGYN Find Cancer Care See an OB-GYN genotypes Order DNA Kits Laboratory evaluations focused on archived formalin-fixed, paraffin-embedded tissue blocks processed through a multiplex real-time polymerase chain reaction assay to identify specific viral genotypes. Valid vaginal lesion genotyping was successfully achieved in 56 women, comprising 30 patients who had a history of prior lower genital tract neoplasia and 26 patients presenting without preceding neoplastic disease. Across all lesions with valid testing results, human papillomavirus genotype 16 predominated, detected in 51.8 percent of cases. Furthermore, statistical analysis demonstrated that human papillomavirus 16 was independently associated with the development of severe VaIN3+ lesions, carrying an adjusted odds ratio of 3.84 with a 95 percent confidence interval of 1.22 to 12.93 and a p-value of 0.024. Direct genotype concordance was specifically assessed in a subset of 28 patients for whom paired tissue specimens from both the original and secondary lesions were available, evaluable, and positive for human papillomavirus. Within this paired group, complete viral concordance was established in 23 women (82.1 percent), partial concordance in four women (14.3 percent), and an absence of concordance in only one woman (3.6 percent). When examining exploratory clinical contrasts, combined positivity for human papillomavirus 16 and 18 occurred more frequently among women with prior neoplasia compared to those without (66.7 percent versus 38.5 percent; p = 0.059), as did VaIN3+ diagnoses (66.7 percent versus 42.3 percent; p = 0.106); however, neither difference remained statistically significant below the 0.05 threshold following adjustment for multiplicity. The research team concluded that the pronounced frequency of shared viral genotypes strongly aligns with long-term viral persistence or subsequent reactivation of the primary human papillomavirus genotype over decades. Nevertheless, the investigators highlighted essential methodological limitations: reinfection with the identical viral genotype over time cannot be definitively excluded, and the analysis did not evaluate whether the paired lesions shared a common clonal origin. Given the extended latency intervals observed between primary and secondary neoplastic diagnoses, the study authors emphasized that these findings reinforce the necessity of extended, long-term surveillance protocols for women who have received treatment for high-grade cervical and lower genital tract lesions. analysis.location_and_population: The research was carried out at University Hospital Královské Vinohrady in Prague, Czech Republic, involving a cohort of 72 women with histologically confirmed and HPV-associated VaIN2+ or higher (N7, N8, N9).
analysis.event: A tissue-based study found that 96.4 percent of evaluable cases shared at least one HPV genotype between initial and subsequent neoplastic sites, with 82.1 percent showing complete concordance (N2, N14, N15).
analysis.scale_impact_and_risk: The study identified 72 women with HPV-associated vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VaIN2+), and 51.8 percent of cases had HPV16 as the predominant genotype. analysis.brief_en: A study published on November 11, 2026, by Bioengineer.org investigated the concordance of human papillomavirus (HPV) genotypes between vaginal neoplasia and prior genital tract lesions. Conducted at University Hospital Královské Vinohrady in Prague, the research analyzed 72 women with histologically confirmed HPV-associated vaginal intraepithelial neoplasia (VaIN2+). Among them, 54.2 percent had a history of prior HPV-related lower genital tract neoplasia. The study found that 96.4 percent of evaluable cases shared at least one HPV genotype between initial and subsequent lesions, with 82.1 percent showing complete concordance. HPV16 was the most common genotype, detected in 51.8 percent of cases, and was independently associated with severe VaIN3+ lesions. The findings suggest a clinical risk of developing VaIN3+ in women with prior HPV-related lower genital tract disease, but the study acknowledges limitations in determining whether the lesions originated from the same virus or new infections. The research team recommends extended long-term surveillance for such patients.

news.content: 新闻 体育 汽车 房产 旅游 教育 时尚 科技 财经 娱乐 HPV16/18到底有多凶?从感染到癌变的完整过程,看完一身冷汗 2026-11-13 16:00 来源: 孚瑞坦 发布于:福建省 在所有诱发宫颈癌的高危型HPV中,HPV16、18是公认的“致癌毒王”。临床数据显示,超70%的宫颈癌病例都与这两种亚型的持续感染相关,它们致病力更强、进展速度更快,是女性宫颈健康的头号隐形威胁。很多人只知道HPV会致癌,却不清楚病毒从入侵到最终引发癌变,究竟经历了怎样的过程。 第一步:黏膜破损入侵,感染毫无症状 HPV病毒不进入血液循环,专挑皮肤黏膜的微小破损处入侵,直达宫颈鳞状上皮的基底层细胞。这个阶段没有任何不适症状,大多数感染者完全不知情。如果自身免疫力足够强,大多数感染会在1-2年内被自然清除,属于一过性感染。 第二步:持续感染形成,病毒实现免疫逃逸 小部分的HPV感染无法被人体自行清除,发展为持续性感染。HPV具备极强的免疫逃逸特性,感染过程中不会触发强烈的免疫反应,病毒可以长期潜伏在细胞内不断复制。当高危型HPV持续感染超过2年,宫颈细胞发生病变的风险会显著升高。 第三步:基因整合,癌变“开关”被激活 HPV16、18的致癌性之所以突出,核心在于其基因整合能力。病毒会将自身基因组嵌入宿主细胞的染色体中,导致调控病毒复制的E2基因失活,解除对E6、E7致癌基因的抑制。大量表达的E6、E7蛋白会分别灭活人体的p53、Rb两大抑癌蛋白,让细胞失去增殖调控,开始无限分裂、异常分化,癌变进程就此正式启动。 第四步:宫颈上皮内瘤变,癌前的预警信号 异常增殖的细胞会逐步引发宫颈上皮内瘤变(CIN),按照病变程度分为CINI、CINII、CINIII三级,级别越高,距离浸润癌越近。这个阶段大多无明显症状,多数患者仅在筛查中发现异常。若在此阶段及时干预,阻断病毒、逆转病变,就能有效阻止癌症发生。 第五步:进展为浸润性宫颈癌 如果CIN阶段未被发现和干预,病变细胞突破上皮基底膜,侵入宫颈间质,就发展为浸润性宫颈癌。此时可能出现接触性出血、不规则阴道流血、异常排液等症状,但往往已错过最佳干预窗口。 从HPV感染到宫颈癌通常需要5-10年甚至更久,这也为临床干预留下了充足的窗口。《中国子宫颈癌三级规范化防治蓝皮书》明确指出,清除高危HPV持续性感染,是无创临床干预的关键时机,既能避免病情进展,也可减少不必要的有创治疗。 针对高危HPV感染的干预,合规有效的医疗器械产品为临床提供了新的选择。孚瑞坦抗人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)凝胶敷料是国家二类医疗器械,采用IgY生物抗体靶向技术,通过“抗体鸡尾酒疗法”多靶点作用:中和清除游离病毒,作用于受感染的宿主细胞,协同改善生殖道环境,可阻断生殖道高危HPV感染、降低病毒载量、防止宫颈病变发生。 一项纳入120例高危HPV感染合并CIN患者的随机对照临床研究显示,使用孚瑞坦抗HPV凝胶敷料治疗后,HPV转阴率可达88.33%,疗效显著优于传统干扰素方案,可有效阻断高危HPV感染进程,为宫颈健康提供可靠防护。[1] HPV感染并不可怕,可怕的是忽视筛查与干预。定期进行HPV分型检测,发现高危感染后及时选择合规、有临床数据支撑的干预方案,是守护宫颈健康的核心关键。 展开全文 品牌简介 孚瑞坦,专业健康品牌,深耕病毒领域。品牌强国医疗器械行业优选成员单位。现产品体系涵盖HPV、HSV等病毒防治需求。拥有以IgY(卵黄免疫球蛋白)为核心的多项专利,致力于用前沿生物科技,惠及全球亿万家庭。 温馨提示:请仔细阅读产品说明书或者在医务人员的指导下购买和使用。本文旨在健康科普,具体诊疗请遵医嘱。 参考文献: [1]苏玲.孚瑞坦抗人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)凝胶敷料治疗高危HPV感染合并CIN的临床疗效分析[J].中文科技期刊数据库(全文版)医药卫生,2024(5):0186-0189返回搜狐,查看更多 阅读 () 平台声明 该文观点仅代表作者本人,搜狐号系信息发布平台,搜狐仅提供信息存储空间服务。

source_language_evidence.brief_en: 新闻 体育 汽车 房产 旅游 教育 时尚 科技 财经 娱乐 HPV16/18到底有多凶?从感染到癌变的完整过程,看完一身冷汗 2026-11-13 16:00 来源: 孚瑞坦 发布于:福建省 在所有诱发宫颈癌的高危型HPV中,HPV16、18是公认的“致癌毒王”。临床数据显示,超70%的宫颈癌病例都与这两种亚型的持续感染相关,它们致病力更强、进展速度更快,是女性宫颈健康的头号隐形威胁。很多人只知道HPV会致癌,却不清楚病毒从入侵到最终引发癌变,究竟经历了怎样的过程。 第一步:黏膜破损入侵,感染毫无症状 HPV病毒不进入血液循环,专挑皮肤黏膜的微小破损处入侵,直达宫颈鳞状上皮的基底层细胞。这个阶段没有任何不适症状,大多数感染者完全不知情。如果自身免疫力足够强,大多数感染会在1-2年内被自然清除,属于一过性感染。 第二步:持续感染形成,病毒实现免疫逃逸 小部分的HPV感染无法被人体自行清除,发展为持续性感染。HPV具备极强的免疫逃逸特性,感染过程中不会触发强烈的免疫反应,病毒可以长期潜伏在细胞内不断复制。当高危型HPV持续感染超过2年,宫颈细胞发生病变的风险会显著升高。 第三步:基因整合,癌变“开关”被激活 HPV16、18的致癌性之所以突出,核心在于其基因整合能力。病毒会将自身基因组嵌入宿主细胞的染色体中,导致调控病毒复制的E2基因失活,解除对E6、E7致癌基因的抑制。大量表达的E6、E7蛋白会分别灭活人体的p53、Rb两大抑癌蛋白,让细胞失去增殖调控,开始无限分裂、异常分化,癌变进程就此正式启动。 第四步:宫颈上皮内瘤变,癌前的预警信号 异常增殖的细胞会逐步引发宫颈上皮内瘤变(CIN),按照病变程度分为CINI、CINII、CINIII三级,级别越高,距离浸润癌越近。这个阶段大多无明显症状,多数患者仅在筛查中发现异常。若在此阶段及时干预,阻断病毒、逆转病变,就能有效阻止癌症发生。 第五步:进展为浸润性宫颈癌 如果CIN阶段未被发现和干预,病变细胞突破上皮基底膜,侵入宫颈间质,就发展为浸润性宫颈癌。此时可能出现接触性出血、不规则阴道流血、异常排液等症状,但往往已错过最佳干预窗口。 从HPV感染到宫颈癌通常需要5-10年甚至更久,这也为临床干预留下了充足的窗口。《中国子宫颈癌三级规范化防治蓝皮书》明确指出,清除高危HPV持续性感染,是无创临床干预的关键时机,既能避免病情进展,也可减少不必要的有创治疗。

news.content: Cambodia launches nationwide HPV campaign to protect girls from cervical cancer-Xinhua Cambodia launches nationwide HPV campaign to protect girls from cervical cancer Source: Xinhua Editor: huaxia 2026-11-11 12:32:45 PHNOM PENH, Nov. 11 (Xinhua) -- Cambodia has launched a nationwide human papillomavirus (HPV) Multi-Age Cohort and catch-up vaccination campaign to expand cervical cancer protection for adolescent girls, according to a joint press release issued Wednesday. Cervical cancer remains a major public health challenge in Cambodia, ranking as the second leading cancer among women of all ages. Because nearly all cervical cancer cases are linked to persistent infection with high-risk strains of HPV, vaccination stands as one of the most effective preventive measures available. Building on the successful integration of the HPV vaccine into Cambodia's National Immunization Program in 2023, the new campaign will run alongside routine vaccinations for nine-year-old girls. The initiative provides free HPV vaccines to all girls aged 13 to 14, while offering catch-up doses for girls aged 10 to 12 who may have missed their routine vaccinations between 2023 and 2025. To maximize coverage, the nationwide campaign will be rolled out in two phases from November to December 2026. At the campaign launch on Tuesday, Cambodian Minister of Health Chheang Ra reaffirmed the country's commitment to protecting future generations. "Every girl deserves protection from cervical cancer," he said. "By expanding HPV vaccination opportunities across the country, we are ensuring that girls who missed previous opportunities can still benefit from this safe, effective, and life-saving vaccine." The campaign will utilize a coordinated approach, delivering vaccines through schools, community centers, and local health facilities. Marianna Trias, the World Health Organization representative to Cambodia, said HPV vaccination is one of the most effective tools for preventing cervical cancer. "By expanding vaccination opportunities for girls up to age 14, Cambodia is accelerating progress towards eliminating cervical cancer while safeguarding the health and well-being of future generations," she said. HPV vaccination is among the most impactful interventions, averting an estimated 13 deaths for every 1,000 children vaccinated, according to the joint press release. Supporting these efforts, Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, has committed substantial financial resources to ensure the initiative's success. "With more than 3 million U.S. dollars in funding for this campaign, which aims to protect more than 700,000 girls in schools and communities, Gavi reaffirms our commitment to support Cambodia in its efforts to build stronger links between adolescent girls and essential health services," said Priya Gajraj, Gavi's director of core countries. ■ Cambodia launches nationwide HPV campaign to protect girls from cervical cancer

The initiative targets girls aged 13 to 14 and offers catch-up doses for those aged 10 to 12 who may have missed previous vaccinations. The campaign will be implemented in two phases from November to December 2026, with vaccines distributed through schools, community centers, and local health facilities. This effort builds on the successful integration of the HPV vaccine into Cambodia's National Immunization Program in 2023. The World Health Organization (WHO) representative, Marianna Trias, emphasized that HPV vaccination is one of the most effective tools for preventing cervical cancer. Gavi, the Vaccine Alliance, has committed over 3 million U.S. dollars in funding to support the campaign, which aims to protect more than 700,000 girls. According to the press release, HPV vaccination is estimated to avert 13 deaths per 1,000 children vaccinated. The campaign is part of Cambodia's broader strategy to safeguard the health of future generations and strengthen links between adolescent girls and essential health services.

news.title: Most Common HPV Strain Shows Lower Lesion Risk in Hospital Study
news.excerpt: A retrospective cross-sectional study of 9,941 hospital patients in Henan, China, revealed that the most common HPV genotype is not the one most strongly linked to high-grade cervical lesions.

While HPV52 emerged as the most prevalent viral type across the patient cohort, its statistical association with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse was not statistically significant. In contrast, HPV16 and HPV18 demonstrated the strongest independent link to high-grade lesions despite being detected less frequently than HPV52. The investigation addressed an important gap in clinical epidemiology surrounding opportunistic hospital testing. China’s organized cervical screening framework targets women aged 35 to 64 years, yet substantial volumes of HPV testing occur opportunistically in tertiary hospital settings among women outside this standard age bracket. Because the genotype-specific and age-stratified epidemiology of this hospital population had remained poorly characterized, researchers analyzed clinical and laboratory records from 2025 to clarify genotype distributions and histological risks. The study cohort comprised 9,941 women aged 14 years or older who underwent genotyping for 23 distinct HPV types, evaluated either alone or alongside liquid-based cytology. Within this overall population, 7,116 individuals presented for opportunistic screening, whereas 2,825 attended for the re-examination of prior abnormal results. Histological diagnoses were available for a subgroup of 850 women, allowing investigators to calculate odds ratios for cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse and establish absolute disease risks using naive calculations paired with verification-bias-adjusted models. Across the entire cohort, overall HPV prevalence was measured at 23.2 percent, with a 95 percent confidence interval spanning 22.3 to 24.0 percent. High-risk HPV prevalence reached 17.8 percent using a standard 14-type assay panel and 16.3 percent when restricted strictly to International Agency for Research on Cancer Group 1 classifications. Clinical context heavily influenced detection rates: women undergoing abnormal-result re-examination exhibited an HPV prevalence of 44.5 percent, roughly three times higher than the 14.7 percent observed among those attending opportunistic screening. Age-specific prevalence displayed a distinct bimodal pattern rather than a continuous decline across older age groups. Positivity peaked at 52.2 percent among individuals aged 20 years or younger, declined to 19.1 percent among women aged 30 to 39 years, and rose again to 40.2 percent among patients aged 60 years or older. Across the cohort, the three most frequently identified genotypes were HPV52, HPV16, and HPV58, highlighting substantial viral diversity across different generations of patients. Among the 850 patients who underwent histological examination, 117 were diagnosed with cervical intraepithelial neoplasia grade 2 or worse, representing 13.8 percent of the biopsied subgroup. More than half of these high-grade cases—54.7 percent—carried HPV16 or HPV18. Multivariate analysis confirmed that HPV16 and HPV18 infection was independently associated with high-grade lesions, yielding an adjusted odds ratio of 10.67 compared to patients negative for all 14 high-risk types. By contrast, the most widespread strain, HPV52, showed a genotype-specific adjusted odds ratio of 1.23, an association that did not achieve statistical significance. Estimates of absolute disease risk per genotype-positive individual further reinforced these divergent clinical trajectories. Modeled absolute risk for high-grade lesions ranged from 18.9 to 32.9 percent for HPV16 and from 9.1 to 18.7 percent for HPV58, while HPV52 conferred an absolute risk range of only 4.3 to 10.2 percent. Sensitivity analyses confirmed that this risk hierarchy remained completely stable after accounting for verification-bias adjustments, demonstrating that frequency of detection does not mirror pathological severity. The study authors concluded that infection rates in this hospital-based setting did not diminish with advancing age, challenging assumptions derived from conventional screening cohorts. Because the most prevalent viral strains differed from those presenting the highest pathological risk, the researchers noted that genotype-specific risk stratification strategies and the upper age boundaries for screening programs warrant rigorous evaluation in future prospective, population-based studies. The findings suggest that genotype-specific risk stratification and screening age boundaries need further evaluation in future studies. supplementary_news.excerpt: A cross-sectional study in Western Province, Zambia, found comparable high-risk HPV rates among younger and older women alongside distinctly different age-related risk determinants.

The study, carried out between October 2025 and January 2026, enrolled 1,132 participants using consecutive sampling to examine the prevalence and determinants of infection. Overall, the researchers detected an HPV prevalence of 33.6 percent, noting virtually identical burdens among younger and older demographics. Specifically, women aged 40 years and younger exhibited an infection rate of 33.6 percent, whereas participants aged 41 years and older had an infection rate of 33.4 percent. To obtain these clinical measurements, healthcare teams collected exfoliated cervical specimens from the participants and screened for high-risk HPV genotypes using the Hologic Panther platform paired with transcription-mediated amplification (TMA). In parallel, investigators administered structured questionnaires to capture detailed sociodemographic, behavioural, and reproductive information from each woman. To account for potential clustering of outcomes across different health facilities in the province, the analytical team applied mixed-effects logistic regression models to identify factors independently associated with viral infection. The statistical analyses revealed that the independent determinants of HPV infection diverged significantly depending on participant age. Among women aged 40 years and younger, infection was independently associated with a higher number of lifetime sexual partners, high parity, lack of HPV vaccination, contraceptive use, low income, single marital status, and attendance at rural healthcare facilities (P < 0.05). In contrast, among women aged 41 years and older, the independent risk factors comprised high parity, low HPV knowledge, unemployment, low income, and broader geographic location (P < 0.05). Beyond age-stratified predictors, the research group documented spatial variations in infection frequency across the study region, observing significantly elevated HPV rates within Mwandi district. The investigators noted that Zambia continues to experience one of the highest cervical cancer burdens globally, where human papillomavirus persists as a leading cause of cervical malignancy in low- and middle-income settings. In interpreting these patterns, the authors indicated that the substantial regional burden of HIV and ongoing transmission dynamics may also play a role in sustaining high levels of HPV infection across age groups. Reflecting on these contrasting associations, the study authors emphasize that interventions should be tailored to address the unique drivers identified within each age demographic. Rather than applying a uniform approach, the findings support integrated, age-specific prevention initiatives that combine HPV vaccination, routine cervical cancer screening, health education, and clinical treatment services to effectively curb the burden of HPV infection and its long-term health consequences across Western Province. supplementary_news.content: HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER Saturday, November 14, 2026 No Result View All Result Login HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER HOME NEWS EXPLORE CAREER Companies Jobs Lecturer PhD Studentship Postdoc Research Assistant EVENTS iGEM News Team PHOTOS VIDEO WIKI BLOG COMMUNITY FACEBOOK INSTAGRAM TWITTER No Result View All Result No Result View All Result Home NEWS Science News Health Lianyungang Study Finds Eighteen Percent Overall Human Papillomavirus Infection Rate by November 12, 2026 in Health Reading Time: 3 mins read 0 Lianyungang Study Finds Eighteen Percent Overall Human Papillomavirus Infection Rate Share on FacebookShare on TwitterShare on LinkedinShare on RedditShare on Telegram A retrospective analysis of 50,279 women at Lianyungang Maternal and Child Health Hospital identified an overall human papillomavirus infection rate of 18.57 percent, representing 9,336 positive cases diagnosed between 2021 and 2025 in Northern Jiangsu Province, China. Longitudinal surveillance over the five-year evaluation period revealed fluctuations in annual detection, with the infection rate rising from 15.30 percent in 2021 to a peak of 21.18 percent in 2023, before adjusting to 19.84 percent by 2025. Evaluation of viral infection patterns indicated that single infections predominated across the positive cohort, accounting for 75.83 percent of cases with 7,080 infected women displaying a single viral genotype. Analysis of age-stratified positivity demonstrated a bimodal distribution across demographic groups, reaching a first peak of 23.56 percent (810 of 3,438) among women aged 25 years or younger and a second peak of 26.05 percent (1,017 of 3,904) among women aged 56 years or older. Genotyping identified HPV52 as the most frequent variant with a prevalence of 3.62 percent (1,822 of 50,279), followed by HPV16 at 3.01 percent (1,514 of 50,279), HPV58 at 2.46 percent (1,239 of 50,279), HPV53 at 1.97 percent (989 of 50,279), and HPV39 at 1.72 percent (864 of 50,279), while HPV81 represented the most prevalent low-risk genotype at 1.70 percent (856 of 50,279). Annual genotype tracking showed that HPV53 prevalence increased significantly from 1.51 percent in 2021 to 2.72 percent in 2025 (P < 0.001), providing the largest localized epidemiological dataset to date to guide regional cervical cancer prevention and control strategies in Lianyungang. The clinical objective of the investigation centered on analyzing both the prevalence and genotype distribution of human papillomavirus infection across the population of Lianyungang, located in Northern Jiangsu Province, China. By systematically characterizing these viral patterns, the research was designed to provide localized epidemiological data necessary to support the prevention and treatment of cervical cancer and related diseases throughout the municipality. To evaluate these dynamics, the study design relied on a retrospective analysis of HPV genotyping records collected from 50,279 women at Lianyungang Maternal and Child Health Hospital between 2021 and 2025. The methodological evaluation systematically examined four distinct epidemiological parameters across the five-year surveillance period: overall infection rates, viral genotype distribution, age-specific positivity across demographic cohorts, and multi-year longitudinal trends. The research team concluded that the investigation provides the largest-scale dataset compiled to date regarding recent human papillomavirus epidemiology in Lianyungang. The authors noted that these localized empirical findings are intended to guide public health authorities in the development and implementation of regional cervical cancer prevention and disease control strategies. In evaluating the composition of positive cases, the researchers observed that solitary viral detection predominated over concurrent strains. The age-stratified data demonstrated that infection risk was concentrated at opposite extremes of the tested demographic spectrum. Women aged 56 years and older recorded the highest positivity rate across all evaluated groups at 26.05 percent (1,017 of 3,904), exceeding the initial peak of 23.56 percent (810 of 3,438) identified among women aged 25 years or younger. Regarding viral heterogeneity across the full sample of 50,279 women, the genotype hierarchy revealed distinct frequencies among dominant variants. HPV52 emerged as the most prevalent genotype at 3.62 percent (1,822 cases), followed by HPV16 at 3.01 percent (1,514 cases) and HPV58 at 2.46 percent (1,239 cases). HPV53 and HPV39 accounted for 1.97 percent (989 cases) and 1.72 percent (864 cases), respectively. In addition to these leading variants, the evaluation specifically classified HPV81 as the most common low-risk human papillomavirus genotype, affecting 1.70 percent of women (856 cases). supplementary_news.content_title: 18岁少女检出18种HPV,高危型占10种!
supplementary_news.content: 新闻 体育 汽车 房产 旅游 教育 时尚 科技 财经 娱乐 18岁少女检出18种HPV,高危型占10种! 2026-11-11 17:33 来源: 知识璞玉 当体检报告上赫然列出‘18种HPV亚型阳性’——其中10种是公认的‘致癌黑手’——连经验丰富的妇科医生都停顿了两秒。这不是科幻片桥段,而是发生在杭州临平区妇幼保健院的真实病例:一位18岁的女孩玲玲,因外阴持续疼痛半月就诊,最终被确诊为外阴尖锐湿疣,同时携带18种人乳头瘤病毒(HPV)亚型,高危型占比高达56%。 HPV不是‘一种病毒’,而是一支‘百变军团’ 很多人误以为HPV是单一病毒,实则它是一个拥有200多个已知亚型的庞大家族。按致癌风险,分为‘低危型’(如6、11型,主要引发尖锐湿疣)和‘高危型’(如16、18、33、45、52、58等,与宫颈癌、阴道癌、肛门癌密切相关)。全球约70%的宫颈癌由HPV16/18型导致,而我国年轻女性中,52、58型感染率甚至超过16型——这正是分型检测不可替代的关键所在。 一次检出18种?不是检测误差,而是免疫防线的‘失守警报’ 临床中,单次检出3–5种HPV亚型已属常见;检出10种以上即提示长期、反复、多途径暴露。玲玲的案例之所以罕见,并非因为‘病毒特别凶猛’,而在于她体内免疫系统未能及时识别并清除——就像一座城市同时遭遇18支不同番号的渗透小队,却迟迟未拉响防空警报。高病毒载量+多亚型共存,恰恰说明感染时间长、局部微环境紊乱、黏膜屏障功能受损,远期发展为CIN2+(高级别宫颈上皮内瘤变)的风险显著升高。 年轻≠安全,但也不等于‘判了死刑’ 值得强调的是:HPV感染不等于宫颈癌,更不等于‘必须切子宫’。数据显示,90%以上的年轻女性在1–2年内可凭借自身免疫力自然清除HPV,尤其在25岁以下群体中,清除率超95%。真正需要警惕的,是‘持续感染’——即同一高危型别在12个月内两次及以上阳性。玲玲的挑战在于‘多重叠加+高危主导’,因此治疗策略必须双线并进:物理祛除可见疣体(如激光/冷冻),同步启动免疫调节(营养干预+生活方式重建),而非盲目使用抗病毒药或过度手术。 给年轻女性的三条硬核建议 第一,别把HPV当成‘性污名标签’——它像感冒病毒一样普遍,一生中约80%的人会感染至少一次;第二,TCT(液基细胞学)和HPV分型必须联合做,单查HPV如同只看‘通缉令’不查‘现场证据’;第三,真正的‘疫苗’不在针管里,而在你的作息表上:睡眠不足4小时,NK细胞活性下降40%;吸烟者HPV清除时间延长3倍;BMI>28者,高危型持续感染风险翻倍。 玲玲正在接受规范治疗,也开启了人生第一次系统性健康管理。她的故事不是恐吓手册,而是一面镜子——照见我们对病毒的误解,也映出身体本就拥有的惊人自愈力。毕竟,最强大的宫颈癌防线,从来不在诊室,而在你规律的晚餐、充足的睡眠,和敢于说‘不’的边界感里。返回搜狐,查看更多 阅读 () 作者声明 含AI生成内容 平台声明 该文观点仅代表作者本人,搜狐号系信息发布平台,搜狐仅提供信息存储空间服务。

supplementary_news.content: メインコンテンツへスキップ Questions to the Diet, Government Answers: What criteria will the government use to decide on routine HPV vaccination for males? Refundable やまと新聞 Nov 9, 2026 18:52 Basic Information Submitting Member: Koichi Mukoyama, Member of the House of Representatives (elected from the Kinki Proportional Representation Block, Parliamentary Group: Democratic Party for the People/Independent Club) Affiliated House: House of Representatives Diet Session: 222nd Diet Session (Extraordinary Session) Question Number: Question No. 10 Question Subject: Written Question Regarding Cost-Effectiveness Analysis for the Routine Vaccination of Males with the HPV Vaccine Submission Date: October 9, 2026 (Reiwa 8) Date Forwarded to Cabinet: October 19, 2026 Date of Answer (Date of Receipt of Written Answer): October 23, 2026 (Cabinet House Question No. 222-10) Introduction: Why is HPV vaccination for males a subject of debate? Human Papillomavirus (HPV) is known as the virus that causes cervical cancer. A supplementary fact sheet from the National Institute of Infectious Diseases (March 2024) states that HPV is also known to cause anal cancer, oropharyngeal cancer, and penile cancer, in addition to cervical cancer. Condyloma acuminatum, a type of benign wart, is also caused by HPV infection. However, not all of these cancers are caused by HPV. On the other hand, which diseases are recognized as being prevented by the vaccine is a separate issue. According to materials from the Ministry of Health, Labour and Welfare's council, the vaccines approved for use in males in Japan are the 4-valent vaccine (2020) and the 9-valent vaccine (August 2025), and the approved indications are for condyloma acuminatum and anal cancer (including its precursor lesions). The prevention of oropharyngeal cancer or penile cancer in males, and the prevention of cervical cancer in females through male vaccination, are not included in the pharmaceutical approvals. Since 2022, the government's council has been deliberating whether to include male vaccination in the 'routine vaccination' program funded by public expenses, but it has not yet reached the stage of routine vaccination. This question addresses the 'cost-effectiveness analysis' presented at the 35th meeting of the council's subcommittee (the Subcommittee on Vaccine Evaluation of the Health Sciences Council's Committee on Immunization and Vaccines, hereinafter 'the Subcommittee') held on July 22 of this year. Cost-effectiveness analysis is a method of numerically evaluating whether the health benefits of a vaccine justify its costs. What kind of lawmaker is the questioner? According to the official House of Representatives member information (as of April 2026), Koichi Mukoyama was born in Itami City, Hyogo Prefecture, in 1957. After graduating from the Faculty of Economics at Osaka University, he worked as an employee of Osaka Gas Co., Ltd., and as a public secretary to a member of the House of Representatives. He served two terms as a Kobe City Council member and two terms as a Hyogo Prefectural Assembly member. As a member of the House of Representatives, he has been elected three times and represents the Kinki Proportional Representation Block. He serves as the representative of the Democratic Party for the People's Hyogo Prefectural Federation and as a director of the House of Representatives Committee on the Environment. As for related past activities, Representative Mukoyama also submitted a 'Written Question Regarding the Early Routine Vaccination of Males with the HPV Vaccine' (Question No. 29) on July 2, 2026, during the previous Diet session (221st Diet Session). In a written answer dated July 14 of the same year, the government stated that it was striving to collect information regarding the effectiveness of routine vaccination. Regarding the motivation for this question, the editorial department could not confirm any materials in which the lawmaker himself explains it on his website or through statements in the Diet. Questions to the Diet: Main Points The written question consists of nine items. supplementary_news.content_title: Scientists Develop Bean-Based Chewing Gum That Traps HPV in 93% of Tested Saliva Samples
supplementary_news.content: No Result View All Result Scientists Develop Bean-Based Chewing Gum That Traps HPV in 93% of Tested Saliva Samples Share Share this article Facebook X LinkedIn Reddit WhatsApp Flipboard Bluesky Email Copy Link Comments Home → Health Scientists Develop Bean-Based Chewing Gum That Traps HPV in 93% of Tested Saliva Samples It traps HPV and kills cancer-associated bacteria. But can it prevent cancer? byTudor Tarita November 13, 2026 in Diseases, Future, Health, News A A A A Reset Edited and reviewed by Mihai Andrei Loading Audio Player By Instaread, Please Wait... Not the actual gum. Credit: Wikimedia Commons A potential new weapon against cancer-linked infections comes in mint flavor; and its secret ingredient comes from an unlikely place: beans. Scientists have developed a chewing gum that might one day help fight cancer-linked infections. And in laboratory tests involving saliva from cancer patients, the results were surprisingly promising. Bean Protein vs. Cancer-Causing Virus HPV is one of the world’s most common sexually transmitted infections. Most infections disappear naturally, but some persist for years. Certain strains can eventually cause cancer, and in the mouth, HPV can create tumors around the tonsils and at the base of the tongue. According to the Centers for Disease Control and Prevention, HPV causes an estimated 60% to 70% of cancers in the back of the throat in the United States. Researchers led by Henry Daniell, a professor at the University of Pennsylvania School of Dental Medicine, wondered whether they could capture HPV particles in the mouth before they infect additional cells or spread to another person. Their solution involved the lablab bean, also called the hyacinth bean. It naturally contains an antiviral protein called FRIL, which binds to sugars on the surfaces of viruses. Lablab purpureus and the resulting gum. Credit: Scientific Reports (2026) Imagine throwing a sticky net over a swarm of insects. This FRIL protein works somewhat similarly, linking virus particles into large clumps that can potentially prevent them from entering human cells. The researchers incorporated this protein into an experimental chewing gum. They then tested extracts from it against HPV in saliva and mouth-rinse samples collected from patients with head and neck cancer. × Get smarter every day... Stay ahead with ZME Science and subscribe. Sign Up Free Daily Newsletter The science you need to know, every weekday. Weekly Newsletter A week in science, all in one place. Sends every Sunday. No spam, ever. Unsubscribe anytime. Review our Privacy Policy. Thank you! One more thing... Please check your inbox and confirm your subscription. After mixing the extracts with the samples, they separated out the viral clumps and measured how much HPV remained in the liquid. The results were striking. HPV particles aggregated in 13 of 14 saliva samples. The extent varied, but several samples showed reductions of more than 85% in detectable HPV after treatment. In HPV-positive mouth-rinse samples, the researchers reported an approximately 80% reduction in the viral signal. In total, the HPV experiments drew on samples from 44 cancer patients. Illustration of how FRIL traps HPV. Credit: Scientific Reports (2026) But why chewing gum rather than a pill? “Oral medicines get diluted in blood and are not suitable for concentrated local delivery at the site of infection,” Daniell told Women’s Health. Chewing gum could release antiviral proteins precisely where they’re needed, rather than distributing them throughout the body. There’s another advantage: the protein comes from a plant that can be cultivated relatively cheaply. And researchers have already developed gum tablets containing the ingredient, rather than merely proposing the idea on paper. A Second Ingredient Goes After Bacteria HPV wasn’t the researchers’ only target. Two bacterial species, Porphyromonas gingivalis and Fusobacterium nucleatum, have also been associated with poorer outcomes in some patients with head and neck cancer. They can promote inflammation and interfere with the body’s defenses, although their precise role in cancer isn’t entirely clear. Fusobacterium. Credit: Wikimedia Commons. The researchers combined the bean gum extract with protegrin-1, an antimicrobial peptide that damages bacterial membranes. The combination proved remarkably potent. After one hour of treatment, it reduced both targeted bacterial species by more than 99% in laboratory-tested patient samples. Interestingly, the treatment appeared to spare some of the mouth’s normal bacterial residents. Certain streptococci, which are commonly found in a healthy oral microbiome, proved more resistant, possibly because protective capsules shield them from the antimicrobial compound. This raises the intriguing possibility of targeting harmful bacteria without wiping out their beneficial neighbors. However, this needs to be investigated in closer detail, the researchers suggest.. Eliminating harmful species without extensively disturbing beneficial ones could be especially valuable for cancer patients, whose treatments sometimes disrupt their oral microbiome. The approach also builds on earlier research from Daniell’s team, which found that bean-derived antiviral chewing gum could neutralize influenza and herpes viruses in laboratory experiments. Could Chewing Gum Actually Prevent Cancer? Credit: Pexels, As encouraging as this is, it’s important to take a step back and look at the big picture. There’s an enormous difference between trapping HPV in a laboratory sample and preventing cancer in a living person. The researchers measured viral aggregation, not whether the gum stopped infections, prevented transmission, or reduced tumor growth. They also don’t know how long any protective effect would last inside the mouth. RelatedPosts This bacterium shoots wires out of its body to power itself Synthetic jellyfish made from rat heart cells can swim like the real deal In Denmark, a Vaccine Is Eliminating a Type of Cervical Cancer Therapeutic vaccine shows promise of treatment against HPV infections that lead to cancer Paolo Serafini, an immunologist at the University of Miami who wasn’t involved in the research, raised precisely this concern. “We do not know how long the gum can take the bacteria and virus away,” Serafini told Women’s Health. “My guess is for an hour. That is not going to have a big impact.” There’s also the question of what happens after the effect wears off. Would pathogens rapidly return? Would people have to chew several pieces every day? And could repeated exposure disturb the delicate balance of microbes that normally inhabit the mouth? And trapping viruses in saliva doesn’t necessarily eliminate infections already established in the tissues of the mouth and throat. A lablab pod. Image via Wiki Commons. HPV vaccination remains the established preventive measure against cancer-causing HPV types. The experimental gum would not replace vaccination, cancer screening, or conventional treatments. Still, Daniell believes the technology deserves clinical testing. In an August interview with the New York Post, he described plans for a four-week trial in which participants would chew the gum three times daily, pending regulatory approval. He also argued that plant-derived proteins could make the treatment unusually inexpensive to manufacture. If human trials confirm that the gum works safely and consistently inside the mouth, it could eventually offer a convenient way to reduce exposure to certain cancer-linked microbes. For now, it’s an inventive laboratory experiment, not a cancer treatment. But the idea is compelling: instead of waiting for a dangerous infection to do damage, perhaps one day we could chew away at the risk. The study was published in the journal Scientific Reports.
